correctness.rationale: For either source equivalence relation, bounded-morphism back to a universal m-world relation makes each equivalence class surject onto the target and hence contain at least m points. With exactly two agents, properness makes intersections of a first-agent class and second-agent class have size at most one. A first-agent class of size at least m therefore meets at least m distinct second-agent classes, each of size at least m, giving at least m^2 source worlds. Equality forces an m-by-m singleton grid, and source labels are bijective on every row and column, giving a Latin square. The cyclic source construction attains the bound.

value.rationale: The source literature uses properization as a recurring bridge from Kripke to simplicial semantics and explicitly flags its representational redundancy. The theorem determines that redundancy exactly in the simplest complete two-agent S5 obstruction, proving the source's quadratic construction is worst-case optimal under the same semantic constraints. The Latin-square equality classification adds reusable combinatorial structure and identifies all optimal designs rather than merely one construction.
